transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to convene us ahead of next Thursday's scheduled closing meeting with Northstar Diagnostics. As you know, we've completed technical diligence on the platform supporting laboratory workflow software and related implementation services, and the current draft grants Northstar distribution rights in North America with standard data-use, revenue-share, export, and conflicts provisions. Northstar is expecting signatures at next Thursday's closing meeting, so I want to make sure we're all comfortable with where things stand. Before I approve the final legal terms, I need to hear from each of you — privacy, finance, export-controls, and conflicts — on whether you have any issues that must be reflected in the agreement before we sign. Let's go through each area systematically.

commitments.detail: Draft and insert a data-use clause prohibiting use of identifiable patient records for model training and requiring deletion exactly 45 days after termination, based on Northstar's proposed data map findings.
Update the revenue-share provision to reflect an 18% share of Northstar's net receipts with quarterly audit rights, based on the benchmark analysis of three comparable laboratory-platform deals.

Update the export provisions to prohibit access by non-U.S. persons and require Northstar to maintain an export-control compliance program, based on the export-classification team's confirmation that the encryption module is controlled technology.

Obtain Northstar's informed written consent to the conflict and implement an ethical screen for the patent-matter team before execution, based on the client-matter database confirmation that Northstar's parent is an existing client in an unrelated patent matter with potentially materially adverse interests.

Once all four updates are reflected in the agreement and the conflicts consent and ethical screen are in place, I will conduct a final review and approve the agreement for signature at or before next Thursday's closing meeting.
